the mishna of 55b cited by the baraita (שהרי שנינו)

props.gloss_en: [the lamb designated for the doubtful firstborn donkey] enters the pen to be tithed
(entertained and rejected) the dictum speaks of the lamb once it has come into the priest's hand
an animal purchased, or given to one as a gift, is exempt from animal tithe
rather, the dictum speaks of an Israelite who has ten doubtful firstborn donkeys in his house
he separates ten lambs for them, tithes them, and they are his
an Israelite who has ten doubtful firstborn donkeys separates ten lambs for them, tithes them, and they are his

an Israelite with ten certain firstborn donkeys inherited from his maternal grandfather the kohen, who had inherited them from his own maternal grandfather the Israelite, separates ten lambs, tithes them, and they are his
an Israelite with smoothed tevel inherited the same way tithes it, and it is his
had he taught only the donkeys, [one would say] there it is because [the lamb] stands separated; but here, gifts not yet separated are as if not separated -- say [the rule does] not [apply]

and had he taught only the tevel, [one would say] it is because it can be tithed from itself, since it lies there; but there, since a lamb must be brought from elsewhere, say not -- so both are needed
one who buys smoothed tevel from a gentile tithes it, and it is his
(entertained) R' Chanina speaks of produce the gentile himself smoothed
'your grain' says the Merciful One -- not the grain of a gentile
rather, an Israelite smoothed it while it was in the gentile's domain
he tithes it, because a gentile has no acquisition in Eretz Yisrael that uproots [produce] from tithe
and it is his, for he says to [the kohen]: I come in the right of a man with whom you cannot litigate
one who deposits his produce with a Kuti or an am haaretz -- it keeps its presumptive status for tithe and for shevi'it
with a gentile -- it is like his [the gentile's] produce
R' Shimon: it is demai
as to separating [teruma and tithes], all agree [he must]
where they disagree is whether to give them to the kohen
the tanna kama holds: [the gentile] certainly exchanged them, and he must give them to the kohen
and R' Shimon holds: demai [whether he exchanged them is in doubt]
perhaps here [the mishna, must give] is teruma gedola, there [R' Chanina, his] is terumat maaser
one who buys smoothed tevel from a gentile is exempt from terumat maaser
as it is said: 'and to the Levites you shall speak and say to them: when you take from the children of Israel'
tevel that you take from the children of Israel -- you separate terumat maaser from it and give it to the kohen
the bridge: tevel that you take from a gentile -- you do not separate terumat maaser from it and give it to the kohen (the case lacks the taking-from-Israelites the verse names)
